name: Equatorial Guinea
snapshot: Ruled since 1979 by Teodoro Obiang, the world's longest-serving president, whose family controls an oil economy that has left most citizens poor.
culture: Equatorial Guinea is the only African country where Spanish is an official language, alongside French and Portuguese. The capital, Malabo, is on Bioko island, home to the Bubi people, while most of the population lives on the mainland, where the Fang are the largest group. Catholic festivals and traditional balélé dances mark the calendar.
society: Oil discovered in the 1990s made the country briefly one of the richest per head in Africa, but wealth was concentrated in the ruling family; the vice-president, Obiang's son, has been convicted in France of embezzlement. Output has declined. Basic services remain poor and press freedom is among the world's lowest.
baseline: Obiang won a sixth term in 2022 with an officially reported 95 percent. His son, Teodoro Nguema Obiang Mangue, known as Teodorín, is vice-president and the presumed successor. In 2025 a scandal involving a senior official secretly filmed with hundreds of women led to arrests and public debate rarely seen in the country.

leaders.state: President Teodoro Obiang Nguema Mbasogo, since 1979
